newsitem.title: FRANCE: France plans study on savings bank reform-paper.
newsitem.headline: France plans study on savings bank reform-paper.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn is planning to launch a study on a reform of the status of state-backed savings banks, the Caisses d'Epargne, financial daily L'Agefi said on Tuesday.
It said the reform would allow the government to use reserves in the Caisses d'Epargne to help reduce the budget deficit.

But given that the study was due to last six months, it was unlikely that the reform would be made on time to provide funds for the 1998 budget, with the money going instead to help bolster 1999 public finances.
Commercial banks have long complained about the privileged status of the Caisses d'Epargne, which enjoys a state guarantee and has a monopoly on the Livret A, a popular tax-free savings account.
Finance ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.
